subject: Urgent: Horizon Health VPC — elevated 500s & p95 latency; tuning request and exec briefing
messages:
From: Sarah Levine <sarah.levine@horizonhealth.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Mike Torres <mike.torres@horizonhealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: High error rate + p95 spike on our private cluster (Horizon Health VPC)

Hi Mina —

We started seeing a jump in 500s and p95 tail latency across our on-prem inference cluster around 07:40 PT this morning. The pattern coincides with a maintenance window where our infra team rolled a kernel patch on the hosts (we were on the recommended kernel from last quarter).

Impact: several production endpoints (triage/notes-generation) are returning 500s intermittently and p95 latency has moved from ~180ms to ~1.9s. This is causing timeouts in our downstream aggregator and visible errors in the clinician UI.

We need urgent triage — can Redwood run a focused investigation and advise whether this is a runtime/kernel interaction, model variant mismatch, or something tunable on your side (batching/KV cache eviction)? Our CTO is watching and we have a maintenance window at 22:00 PT tonight for remediation.

Attached: horizon-slo-extract.csv (SLO violations snapshot).

Thanks,
Sarah
SRE, Horizon Health

Attachment: horizon-slo-extract.csv (CSV, 14KB)

Sarah — quick triage notes from the runtime side after looking at the logs you uploaded to the shared Drive (thanks):

Observations:
- Repeated "KV cache eviction" warnings around 07:38 followed by increased token generation latency for sequences >1024 tokens. That coincides with a host-level kernel update (you mentioned the maintenance window).
- Several worker processes show "illegal instruction" traces on a subset of hosts (two of your hosts may be running a different microcode/AVX level post-patch) — this can cause slow fallbacks into software kernels for matmul.
- We see higher lock contention on mmap regions when multiple processes attempt to share quantized model artifacts.

Immediate asks (what we need from your SREs):
1) onprem-kernel-profiles.log (kernel dmesg + perf samples) — your SRE uploaded a truncated file; need full.
2) output of ./repro-script.sh I’m attaching — it runs a short profiler that exercises the same model and surface kernel fallbacks.

Proposed remediations (short-term):
- Pin runtime to the previous kernel ABI for the affected hosts (rollback) OR apply our runtime fallback patch (we can push a non-disruptive patch if you prefer).
- Increase KV cache size and enable conservative cache eviction while we stabilize (config change, no deploy).
- Temporarily reduce max sequence length on production route to 1024 to avoid triggering slow kernels.

Rishi
Senior Runtime SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: repro-script.sh (shell), initial-kernel-diff.txt

Subject: Internal & external summary — Horizon Health VPC: root cause hypothesis and immediate action items (exec brief)

Team / Horizon execs — short executive summary and plan. I’m sending this both as the customer-facing update and the internal coordination note.

Executive summary (2 lines):
- Impact: ~2% 500s and p95 latency regression to ~1.9s for long sequences across 3 hosts after a kernel microcode/ABI change. Clinician workflows are affected; Horizon has requested urgent remediation.
- Root cause (hypothesis): Kernel microcode/ABI change post-maintenance caused a subset of hosts to fall back to slower software kernels for AVX/FP paths and increased mmap lock contention affecting KV cache behavior.

Immediate actions (next 8 hours):
1) Config mitigation (ASAP, low risk): reduce max_seq_length to 1024 for the affected route; increase KV cache allocation by 20%. (Rishi to apply and verify)
2) If config mitigation insufficient (within 4 hours): rollback kernel on affected hosts or apply Redwood runtime micro-patch that forces the optimized native kernels off the fallback path. (Marcus to coordinate with Horizon infra)
3) Post-mortem & prevention: capture full perf traces for each host, add kernel compatibility check in our onboarding checklist, and add an automatic Canary for kernel/AVX mismatch. (Evelyn to own post-mortem)

Customer comms plan:
- Mina to send a short status update to Horizon CTO in 30 minutes with the mitigation plan and ETA for verification.
- If we cannot verify improvement within 4 hours, propose a controlled rollback in the 22:00 PT window.

Attachments provided by customer: onprem-kernel-profiles.log
Attachments we provided: repro-script.sh, initial-kernel-diff.txt

Thanks — Mina
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
